title: Modules: Sources, Versions and the Registry

header.html: 5a Explain how Terraform sources modules; 5d Manage module versions
the official Terraform Associate (004) exam content list

html:
1What a module is

A module is a container for several resources that are used together: a folder of .tf files. Modules organize, encapsulate and reuse configuration.

Term Meaning
Root module The configuration in the working directory where you run Terraform
Child module A module called by another module with a module block
Published module A module shared through a registry 
module "network" {
  source  = "terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws"
  version = "~> 5.0"

  name = "app-network"
  cidr = "10.0.0.0/16"
}
Exam tip

. Every Terraform configuration is a module: the one you run is the root module.

2Module sources

The source argument tells Terraform where to get the module. It is required.

Source Example source value
Local path ./modules/network or ../shared/network (must start with ./ or ../)
Terraform Registry (public) terraform-aws-modules/vpc/aws (namespace/name/provider)
Private registry (HCP Terraform) app.terraform.io/my-org/network/aws
GitHub github.com/my-org/terraform-aws-network
Generic Git git::https://example.com/network.git?ref=v1.2.0
HTTP URL An archive at a URL
Cloud storage S3 or Google Cloud Storage buckets
Fact Detail
Download terraform init downloads modules into .terraform/modules
After a source change Run terraform init again (or terraform get)
Registry naming Modules are named terraform-<PROVIDER>-<NAME>
Verified modules The public registry marks modules reviewed by HashiCorp partners

3Module versions

Source type How to pin a version
Registry modules (public or private) The version argument with the same constraint syntax as providers (~> 5.0, >= 5.1, < 6.0, = 5.2.0)
Git A tag, branch or commit with ?ref=
Local paths No version: the files are whatever is on disk

The version argument works only with registry sources. Without it, Terraform uses the newest version on the first init.

Practice Why
Pin module versions Predictable infrastructure
Upgrade on purpose Change the constraint and run terraform init -upgrade
Use semantic versions Major changes may break, minor add, patch fix
Exam tip

. version is for registry modules only. For a Git module use ?ref=; for a local module there is no version.

4Why use modules

Benefit Meaning
Reuse Write once, call many times with different inputs
Encapsulation Hide details behind inputs and outputs
Consistency Same standards everywhere
Speed Start from tested modules in the registry
Organization Smaller, focused configurations
Exam tip

. A module needs init before it works. Whenever a module block is added or its source changes, run terraform init again.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which source value refers to a module in a folder next to the root configuration?

  • Amodules/network (no prefix)
  • B./modules/network
  • Cnetwork.local
  • Dfile:network
Show the answer

Answer: B. Local paths must begin with ./ or ../.

S2A team wants to pin a public registry module to any 5.x version. What should they add to the module block?

  • Aref = "5.x" in the module block
  • Bbranch = "5"
  • Cversion = "~> 5.0"
  • Dtag = "v5"
Show the answer

Answer: C. The version argument takes a constraint such as ~> 5.0 and works for registry modules.

S3Which command downloads the modules of a configuration?

  • Aterraform init
  • Bterraform fmt
  • Cterraform output
  • Dterraform show
Show the answer

Answer: A. terraform init downloads modules into the .terraform/modules directory.

S4A module comes from a Git repository. How can a team pin it to a release tag?

  • AWith ?ref= in the source address
  • BWith the version argument of the module
  • CWith the lifecycle block
  • DWith a provider alias
Show the answer

Answer: A. For Git sources the ref query parameter selects a tag, branch or commit.

S5What is the root module?

  • AThe first module published to the registry
  • BThe module with the most resources
  • CThe module that holds the state
  • DThe configuration in the working directory
Show the answer

Answer: D. The root module is the configuration in the directory where Terraform runs.

S6Which statement about the version argument is correct?

  • AIt works for registry modules only
  • BIt works for local path modules
  • CIt works for Git modules
  • DIt works for every source type listed
Show the answer

Answer: A. The version argument is only valid for modules from a registry.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What is a module?

Show the answer

A container of resources used together, in a folder.

R2What argument is required in a module block?

Show the answer

source.

R3What must a local path start with?

Show the answer

./ or ../

R4Where are downloaded modules stored?

Show the answer

.terraform/modules.

R5Which sources accept the version argument?

Show the answer

Registry sources only.

R6How do you pin a Git module?

Show the answer

With ?ref= in the source address.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Module folder of .tf files; root module is the working directory
Sources local path, registry, private registry, GitHub, Git, HTTP, S3, GCS
Versions version for registry modules only; ?ref= for Git; none for local
Commands init downloads modules; init -upgrade moves to newer versions
